It’s a lighter take on creamy potatoes. The potatoes cook in beef broth instead of milk or cream, which means they’re not as heavy, but still just as delicious as their dairy-laden potato gratin counterparts.

There are only 5 ingredients. All you need is potatoes, beef broth, cheese, butter, and garlic (and salt and pepper). The recipe is simple, but we promise flavorful, tender potatoes with a golden-brown, cheesy crust.

Child’s version layers sliced onions with the potatoes, but I saw other recipes that just had potatoes, which I prefer (if you love onions, try our French onion scalloped potatoes instead). I adapted Julia’s recipe, making a larger amount to feed a crowd and trying different amounts of cheese to find what I liked best. This version is loaded with tender potatoes, which soak up flavorful beef broth, all crowned with a crispy, cheesy top. It’s just as delicious as traditional scalloped potatoes, but lighter because the sauce doesn’t contain any milk or cream. It’s still cozy, comforting, and all the things you want in a potato casserole.

“Oh boy, were these delicious. This is a great example of a recipe that is very simple, but every ingredient is really working hard. The potatoes come out super-tender and highly flavorful, having cooked in broth, and the Gruyère adds a creamy bite without being overwhelming. I want to make this for every holiday instead of the traditional mash.” —Andrea, October 2026

After going to culinary school in Paris, I learned how to test and develop recipes at America’s Test Kitchen. I’ve created hundreds of recipes over the past 20 years, and with each one I keep the home cook in mind to make sure each recipe is foolproof and something they’ll want to make over and over again.
Potatoes: Grab starchy russet potatoes (also our choice for the fluffiest mashed potatoes) here because they’ll absorb the broth as they get tender, and their starch helps to thicken the sauce.
Beef broth: Use full-salt beef broth to make sure the potatoes are well-seasoned.

Gruyère cheese: This nutty Swiss cheese browns beautifully after it melts and gives some richness and depth to the gratin. Most blocks at the store are 6 or 8 ounces, and either will work here (although I always vote for more cheese!).

Layer the ingredients. In a baking dish, layer half of the sliced potatoes, cheese, butter, and pepper. Top with the remaining potatoes.
Heat the broth. Bring beef broth and salt to a boil. Pour over the potatoes.
Finish layering. Sprinkle the remaining cheese, butter, and pepper over the top. Doing this last means that they’ll stay in place rather than shifting around when the broth is poured on.

Bake and cool. Bake until the potatoes in the center are tender. Let cool for 15 minutes before serving so the sauce can thicken slightly. The sauce won’t be as thick as potato gratins made with dairy, but it will still be delicious!
This easy cheesy potato gratin is super-flavorful because the potatoes cook in broth.
3 pounds russet potatoes (6 medium or 4 large)
6-8 ounces Gruyère cheese, shredded (1 1/2 to 2 cups) and divided
4 tablespoons unsalted butter, diced and divided, plus more for the baking dish
1/4 teaspoon freshly ground black pepper, divided
Chopped fresh parsley leaves, for garnish (optional)

Arrange a rack in the top third of the oven and heat the oven to 375ºF. Rub the cut sides of 1 peeled garlic clove on the bottom and sides of a 9x13-inch baking dish, then discard the garlic. Coat the baking dish generously with unsalted butter.
Peel 3 pounds russet potatoes, then cut crosswise with a chef’s knife or on a mandoline into thin (1/8-inch-thick) slices.

Arrange half of the potato slices in the baking dish in an even layer. Sprinkle with half of the shredded Gruyère cheese (3 to 4 ounces), 2 tablespoons of the diced unsalted butter, and 1/8 teaspoon of the black pepper. Repeat layering the remaining potato slices.

Bring 2 1/3 cups beef broth and 1/2 teaspoon kosher salt to a boil in a small saucepan over high heat. Evenly pour over the potatoes. Sprinkle with the remaining shredded Gruyère cheese, 2 tablespoons diced unsalted butter, and 1/8 teaspoon black pepper.

Bake until the potatoes in the center are very knife-tender and the top is golden-brown, 65 to 70 minutes. Let cool for 15 minutes for the sauce to thicken slightly. Garnish with chopped fresh parsley leaves if desired.
Storage: Leftovers can be refrigerated in an airtight container for up to 4 days.
